structure: Missouri K-5 Grade-Level Expectations (Spring 2016) as a Word document made of 14 tables. Seven numbered strands (1 Principles of constitutional democracy documents; 2 Principles and processes of governance systems; 3a Continuity and change in history of Missouri and the US; 4 Economic concepts; 5 Geography; 6 Relationships of individuals and groups; 7 Tools of social science inquiry) each introduced by a title cell ('N. Knowledge of ...'), then a header row 'CONCEPTS | GRADE K | GRADE 1 | ... | GRADE 5'. Each concept is lettered (A., B., ...) and takes two table rows: a row whose first cell is the letter and whose other cells are the grade expectations, then a row repeating the same expectations with the concept name in column 1 (e.g. 'Purposes and principles of the Bill of Rights'); both rows are standards and carry identical text. Grade is given by the header-row column (the C index of each cell equals the C index of its GRADE header; header C positions differ between header rows/tables because of merged cells, so each cell is mapped to the header row of its own block). Empty grade cells mean the concept is not taught in that grade. Column-1 cells (letter, concept name, strand title, CONCEPTS) apply to all of K-5. No separate example blocks, front matter or appendices: 'See teacher resources for illustrative examples' is embedded inside the standard text and stays with the standard. Table 6 (strand 4 concept D) has no header row of its own and continues the strand-4 block with the standard K..5 = C2..C7 layout. Only front matter is the nondiscrimination statement (u1) plus a stray 'aaaa' paragraph at the end (u584).
